thread.title: Apple Stock Faces ‘Sell The News’ Curse With iPhone Launch

author: PATRICK SEITZ
title: Apple Stock Faces ‘Sell The News’ Curse With iPhone Launch
text:
Will Apple ( AAPL ) stock stick to tradition and tumble on Wednesday after it introduces its latest lineup of iPhones?
X It's a pretty good bet. Shares of the tech icon tend to rise ahead of a new iPhone introduction as anticipation builds for what the new product will bring. Then Apple stock usually drops on the day of the launch event, following the old Wall Street saying, "Buy the rumor, sell the news."
For the past 10 iPhone introductions, since the original handset, Apple stock has fallen on average 0.4% on the day of the unveiling. It has fallen on eight of the last 10 iPhone launch days.
Last year, when Apple debuted the iPhone 8 series and iPhone X, Apple stock dipped 0.4% for the day. So it's likely to fall after Wednesday's unveiling, if it follows the pattern.
The numbers are even worse during the full week of a new iPhone launch. After the past 10 iPhone introductions, Apple stock has fallen on average 1.8% for the full week.
But its performance has been trending upward. Last year, Apple rose 0.8% for the full week after the iPhone 8/X launch. It has risen in four of the last six iPhone launch weeks.
New iPhones, Apple Watch Expected Analysts expect Apple to introduce three 12th-generation iPhones at it annual fall product launch event , being held at the company's Cupertino, Calif., headquarters. It starts at 10 a.m. local time and is being webcast. They predict an updated version of the 5.8-inch OLED-screen iPhone X, a 6.5-inch OLED model and a 6.1-inch LCD-screen handset.
The new smartphones are likely to be called the iPhone XS series, according to tech media reports. The phones are said to sport faster processors, better cameras and all support Face ID technology for unlocking the device.
Analysts also expect Apple to launch its fourth-generation smartwatch at the event. Other new products could include second-generation AirPods wireless earbuds, as well as new iPad tablets and Mac computers.
Three Price-Target Hikes For Apple Stock Three Wall Street firms raised their price targets on Apple stock on Monday and Tuesday: Loop Capital Markets, S&P Equity Research and UBS.
Loop analyst Ananda Baruah reiterated his buy rating on Apple and upped his price target to 256 from 220. Apple rose 2.5% to 223.85
"While the stock has clearly run ahead of Apple's Wednesday 9/12 event, and as such could digest recent gains after the announcement, we nonetheless believe Apple has a handful of catalysts at its back, and should be able to maintain them for the foreseeable future," he said in a note to clients.
UBS analyst Timothy Arcuri kept his buy rating and hiked his price target on Apple stock to 250 from 215.
Arcuri said he is incrementally more positive on the prospects for iPhone upgrades and services growth.
